written.description: Gives an agent a browser that controls its own network traffic, so the model can capture, edit, replay and compare the requests a web app sends without a proxy in between. Each session runs under a network policy and records every fetch it allowed or refused.

alive.last_commit_message:
h5i-app-std: add a proven HashMap without new axioms (#715)

A hash map written in the Aeneas subset (`Vec<Vec<(K, V)>>` buckets) and
extracted like the rest of the crate, so it is verified rather than modeled.

- `hashmap::HashMap`: new, with_capacity, default, get, contains_key,
  insert, remove, len, is_empty, from_vec. Fixed bucket count, no rehash.
- `KeyHash` replaces `std::hash::Hash` (no hasher, no random seed), with
  impls for u8, u32, u64, usize, bool and Vec<u8> (FNV-1a). Composite keys
  are derived-PartialEq structs: Aeneas models the tuple `==` as an axiom.
- `H5iAppLib.Buckets`: hash-agnostic lemmas on buckets as maps.
- `StdSpecs`: a `@[step]` spec for every operation, stated over
  `hashmap.lookup` (the `mapGet` of the entries) under `hashmap.Inv`. The
  specs only ask that `key_hash` never fail (`HashModel`), not that it
  avoid collisions. `HashModel.ofTotal` covers a kernel's own impls.
- `insert` moves `k` and `v` in both arms: a drop flag made the extraction
  inside a kernel differ from the crate's own, and the specs must fit both.

Checked with `h5i app check` (standard axioms only) and with a scratch
kernel that includes h5i_app_std with `std-specs = true`.
